overall_diagnosis: The recurring issue is confined to maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md and concerns missing or overly broad guidance for diagnosing and repairing dependency-resolution failures in nested or integration-test Maven projects (such as Maven Invoker projects, src/it fixtures, or plugin-driven embedded builds). Current workflow guidance emphasizes reproducing CI but does not clearly distinguish failures originating in the main reactor versus nested test builds, nor does it constrain repair scope. This can lead to incorrect global dependencyManagement or parent-POM changes when the proper fix is localized to the nested test project or its invoking plugin configuration.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill lacks explicit workflow guidance for nested/integration-test Maven projects that resolve dependencies independently from the main reactor. It does not clearly explain how to identify nested builds in logs, reproduce them separately, inspect nested POMs/effective dependency trees, or determine whether dependency failures belong to the root reactor or a nested test fixture. The absence of scoped repair rules risks overly broad fixes such as editing parent dependencyManagement, global plugin versions, or unrelated production modules when only an embedded test project is failing.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a dedicated subsection covering nested and Invoker-based integration-test projects. Explain how to detect nested builds (e.g., maven-invoker-plugin, src/it projects, separate Maven executions during verify), reproduce them independently, and inspect their effective POMs and dependency trees. Clarify that nested test projects may maintain independent dependencies, repositories, and plugin configurations from the main reactor. Add explicit repair-scoping guidance: prefer localized fixes in the nested test project POM, repository configuration, parent resolution, or invoking plugin setup before modifying top-level dependencyManagement or shared plugins. Include common nested-project remedies such as ensuring required repositories are visible to the nested build, aligning plugin-provisioned local repositories, validating relativePath/parent configuration, and preserving historical CI/JDK constraints instead of applying broad modernization changes.
